bestPractices: Pin all session logic to America/New_York explicitly via hour(time,"America/New_York") so Asia 20:00, London 02:00-05:00, NYAM 09:30-12:00, NYPM 13:30-16:00 are chart-tz-independent (sample 09:2115).
Use a generic f_inSession(h,m,startH,startM,endH,endM) helper that handles wrap-around (start<end vs start>end) — sample 09:2106-2113.
Add Silver Bullet sub-zones (10:00-11:00, 14:00-15:00) as optional toggles alongside main killzones, all sharing one bgcolor() dispatcher (sample 09:264-271, 2119-2131).
Anchor midnight-open hour to syminfo.timezone offset correction (Chicago → hour 23) for assets on CME tz (sample 09:99).
Keep killzone bg color transparent (~90%) so candles remain readable.
commonMistakes: Hardcoding session hours in chart-local time — repaints/wrong zone when user changes exchange tz or DST flips.
Using naive 'and minute==0' instead of >= / < minute totals — misses or duplicates boundary bars.
Only defining Asia/London/NY and skipping Silver Bullet / London Close — incomplete ICT killzone set.
No wrap-around handling for Asia 20:00-00:00 → false negatives at midnight.
Mixing bar_time strings like "0830-0831:123456" without stating the tz arg → ambiguous.

bestPractices: All HTF request.security() calls pass lookahead=barmerge.lookahead_off and gaps=barmerge.gaps_on (sample 07:110-115, 377) — no future leak.
Compute TA (crossover, highest, atr) in HTF context inside the security call tuple then ship results, instead of shipping raw HTF close and computing on LTF (sample 07:208 htfSetupDetection()).
Gate confirmations on barstate.isconfirmed so structure/sweep/break only fire on bar close — sample 09 uses AlertFlags non-var object reset per tick but confirms only on close (09:2150-2161).
For DOL/NWOG/NDOG use request.security_lower_tf on M1 with hour()/minute() checks against America/New_York to detect 16:14 / 18:00 closes precisely (sample 09:1383-1412).
Pass pivots as na except on confirm bar (ta.pivothigh returns na) and only act when not na — natural anti-repaint (sample 09:2921-2924).
commonMistakes: Using lookahead=barmerge.lookahead_on for HTF close then trading on it — repaints the signal bar.
Shipping raw HTF high/low and doing crossover logic on LTF — produces mid-bar flicker signals.
Running sweep/BOS detection inside the live (unconfirmed) bar without barstate.isconfirmed gate → marks appear/disappear intrabar.
Recomputing HTF bias every tick via request.security without caching — heavy + inconsistent.
Using barmerge.gaps_off (default) on lower-timeframe pivots → na propagation wrong, phantom pivots.

bestPractices: Two-phase state machine: phase 0 = armed, phase 1 = wick pierced (high>lvl and close<lvl for BSL; low<lvl and close>lvl for SSL), phase 2 = confirmed by close back through confirmLevel (sample 09:2164-2188 f_sweepTick).
Add confirmBars timeout: if reversal doesn't confirm within N bars, re-arm phase=0 — prevents stale sweep flags (sample 09:2179).
confirmLevel set to the sweep bar's opposite extreme (low for BSL sweep, high for SSL) — proper Turtle Soup reject threshold.
Per-level SweepState UDT threaded by-reference so the same engine serves Session H/L, PD/PW/PM, EQH/EQL uniformly (sample 09:2142-2148).
Sweep detection runs even when the level class is display-hidden (Dashboard still reads mitigation) — sample 09:2360-2368.
commonMistakes: Treating any wick through a level as a sweep with no body-close confirmation — huge false positives.
No re-arm timeout → one wick keeps firing alerts forever.
Coupling sweep logic to each level type (PDH, EQH, session high) instead of a shared engine — duplication + drift.
Only marking sweeps, no mitigation state on the level line — loses context.
Drawing the marker inside detection fn without gating by show flag — visual spam when many levels.

bestPractices: BOS vs CHoCH via close-break that must HOLD N bars (struct_holdBars): phase 0→1 on close>lvl, phase 1→2 confirmed if still outside after holdBars, phase 1→3 trap if close back inside (sample 09:2282-2299 f_bosTick).
Track struct_trend state machine: BOS continues trend, CHoCH flips it; lastBreak label distinguishes (sample 09:2274-2275, 2312-2322).
Distinguish wick-pierce (sweep) from body-close (BOS) explicitly — sweeps feed sweep engine, BOS/CHoCH feed structure engine.
Allow configurable pivot length independent of sweep/EQHL pivot length (struct_pivotLen vs eqhl_pivotLen — sample 09:2255).
Mitigation state tracked at barstate.isconfirmed only — anti-repaint (sample 09:2361).
commonMistakes: Using high/low break instead of close for BOS — counts wick taps as structure breaks (sample 07 useHighLow input defaults false, the right default).
Confirming BOS on the same bar it broke → intrabar repaint; no holdBars gate.
No trap detection (close back inside) — labels a failed break as valid BOS.
Single pivot length shared across structure/EQHL/sweep — tuning one breaks others.
Not separating BOS (continuation) from CHoCH (reversal) — loses bias-flip signal.

bestPractices: Standard 3-candle gap: bullish FVG top=low[0], bottom=high[2]; bearish top=low[2], bottom=high[0] (sample 09:507-508, 534-535).
Box anchored bar_index-2 left, bar_index right, then extended forward (extendfvgbox) only while unmitigated — sample 09:522, 680-689.
Mitigation modes selectable: Engulf (body through both sides), Mitigate (wick touches), Rebalance (close inside erased) — sample 09:224-225, 682-689.
Optional VI-anchor: when a Volume Imbalance overlaps the same 3 candles, tighten FVG top/bottom to the VI body gap (sample 09:208-209, 509-514, 631-639) — removes phantom wide FVG.
Liquidity Void mode: consecutive same-direction FVGs merge into one LV box (sample 09:563-613).
Box cap (fvgMaxBoxSet) with array.shift + box.delete to bound drawings (sample 09:525-528).
commonMistakes: Building FVG from high[1]/low[1] instead of low[0]/high[2] — wrong gap geometry.
Left-anchoring box at bar_index (current bar) instead of bar_index-2 — box starts late, covers wrong candles.
No mitigation mode toggle — either over-mitigates on wick touch or never marks mitigation.
No VI-anchor → wide overlapping FVG+VI boxes that visually conflict.
Not deleting boxes when capped → Drawing limit exceeded, indicator stops rendering.
Treating inverse/Implied FVG same as classic FVG — different geometry (needs engulf).

bestPractices: IFVG requires ENGULF of prior candle plus wick criteria: high[0]>high[2], low[2]<low[0], partial overlap (low[0]<=high[2]), body-dominant both sides (>50% body vs wick), and mid-price cross condition (sample 09:642 isBuIFvg, 644 isBeIFvg).
Box anchored at the IMPLIED gap midpoint: top=(min(open,close)+low)/2, bottom=(high[2]+max(open[2],close[2]))/2 — sample 09:648.
Separate mitigation type for IFVG (ifvgmitigationtype Engulf/Mitigate) independent of FVG (sample 09:225).
IFVG only plots when showifvg AND Inversefvgmode toggles both off/on controlled — sample 09:206-207, 517-521.
Alert event tagged 'I.FVG+' / 'I.FVG-' distinct from 'FVG+' (sample 09:653, 661).
commonMistakes: Treating any 3-candle imbalance as IFVG without engulf requirement — IFVG loses meaning.
Reusing FVG box geometry for IFVG — wrong top/bottom, misses the 50% body rule.
No separate mitigation logic for IFVG → it never mitigates or mitigates too early.
Not gating Inverse vs Implied (two different concepts) — confusion, both fire.
Skipping the mid-price cross check (line 642 last conditions) → false IFVG on simple overlaps.

bestPractices: Two tiers: internal OB (last down-candle before bullish BOS) and swing OB (last down-candle before swing BOS) with separate sizes/filters (sample 12:98-101, 20:99-102).
Filter volatile OBs via ATR or Cumulative Mean Range method (orderBlockFilterInput ATR/RANGE — sample 12:102, 20:103).
Mitigation selectable: CLOSE (close through OB) vs HIGHLOW (wick through) — sample 12:103, 20:104.
Body vs full candle OB: useBody toggle (LuxAlgo sample 09-derived 12 use max=min(open,close) vs high/low — sample 13:131-132).
OB drawn as box with break-color state (bullBrkCss/bearBrkCss) once mitigated (sample 13:54-57).
Alert on OB FORMATION with symbol+bias+internal/swing+time (sample 20 modified header).
commonMistakes: Defining OB as 'last opposite candle' with no structural break requirement → every opposite candle becomes OB, chart flooded.
No volatility filter → tiny range candles flagged as OB, low-probability setups.
Mitigating OB on wick touch when user expects close-through (or vice versa) — wrong default.
Single OB tier only — misses the internal/swing confluence hierarchy.
Not separating break (mitigated) color from fresh OB color — can't see which OBs are still live.
Hardcoding OB lookback length instead of input — non-adaptive.

bestPractices: Two correlated symbols via request.security (ES1!, YM1!) on same timeframe, raw pivots computed unconditionally (sample 09:2791-2793, 2921-2937).
Pivot-pair divergence: two synced swing points (within window = pivotLen × pairMult bars) compared to previous synced point — product of deltas < 0 = divergence (sample 09:2857-2859).
Two scales: short pivot (5) and long pivot (25), each with own window multiplier so long tolerates wider gaps (sample 09:2794-2796, 2925-2926).
Level-break SMT: one symbol breaks its OWN long-scale reference while the other holds for holdBars — both break = not divergence (sample 09:2880-2918 f_smtBreak).
Alert per event: 'SMT BEAR ES1!' vs 'SMT BREAK BULL YM1!' tagged with breaker name (sample 09:2867, 2917).
UDT SmtPair/SmtBreak threaded by-reference, one detector per (symbol,side,scale).
commonMistakes: Comparing chart pivots to correlated symbol pivots without syncing window → pairs any two random pivots.
Single scale only → misses HTF SMT divergence context.
Both-break not filtered → labels correlated moves as divergence.
Using close instead of raw pivot high/low for divergence → smoothed, lagging.
No max divergence cap → drawing limit blown, indicator freezes.
Hardcoding correlated symbol instead of input.symbol → can't reuse for ES/NQ/YM.

bestPractices: HTF bias = EMA fast>slow (htfBullish/htfBearish) computed in HTF context, shipped to LTF (sample 07:117-118).
HTF setup state machine with timeout: htfSetupBull/Bear flag + htfSetupBar + htfSetupHigh/Low + setupTimeout bars (sample 07:157-180).
Require HTF BOS/MSS confluence for setup (requireHTFStructure input — sample 07:23).
HTF SL/TP method selectable: HTF Structure / HTF ATR / HTF Swing (sample 07:69-71).
LTF entry only fires when HTF setup active + LTF confirmation + confluence count >= minConfluences (sample 07:74-75).
State vars declared var so they persist across bars; detection fn returns tuple shipped via security (sample 07:158-162, 208).
commonMistakes: Recomputing HTF bias every LTF bar via request.security inline → flicker, repaint.
No setup timeout → stale HTF setup triggers entries hours later when context gone.
LTF entry without HTF confluence gate → trades against HTF bias.
Shipping HTF close then computing bias on LTF → lookahead contamination if lookahead_on, lag if off-and-uncached.
Single EMA cross as bias with no structure confirmation → choppy bias flips.
Not persisting setup state (using non-var) → reset every bar, no memory of setup.

bestPractices: Single _wh_json(event,high,low) builder returning a flat JSON string with event, ticker (syminfo.ticker), exchange (syminfo.prefix), timeframe (timeframe.period), price_high, price_low, close, time (str.format_time in America/New_York) — sample 09:42-43.
Use alert() (dynamic) not alertcondition() so payload can vary per event; user selects 'Any alert() function call' in TV dialog (sample 09:35 tooltip).
Granular enable toggles per category: formations / mitigations / sweeps / structure / smt (sample 09:36-40).
Frequency discipline: formations use alert.freq_once_per_bar_close (no intrabar spam), mitigations/sweeps/SMT-break use alert.freq_once_per_bar (sample 09:531 vs 2205).
Distinct event tags: FVG+, FVG-, I.FVG+, LV+, GAP+, SWEEP ...BSL, BOS ...BSL, CHoCH ..., SMT BEAR/BULL, SMT BREAK — parseable by orchestrator (sample 09 throughout).
Numeric fields formatted with format.mintick for precision consistency (sample 09:43).
commonMistakes: Using alertcondition() with fixed message → can't embed runtime price/time/symbol, no JSON.
Putting alert() inside if without barstate.isconfirmed → fires on every tick of the forming bar.
Same freq for formations and mitigations → either spam or missed fast mitigation events.
No event taxonomy — orchestrator can't distinguish FVG from OB from sweep.
Missing ticker/timeframe/exchange → webhook consumer can't route multi-symbol.
Time in chart tz instead of America/New_York → inconsistent timestamps across users.
No enable toggle → user gets all alerts or none, can't filter by category.

bestPractices: Per-array caps with shift+delete: fvgMaxBoxSet, eqhl_maxPools, struct_maxBreaks, smt_maxDiv, ho_maxLines — bounded drawings (sample 09:222, 2308-2311, 2815).
Declare indicator max_lines_count=500, max_boxes_count=500, max_labels_count=500, max_bars_back=5000 upfront (sample 09:14-18).
Set behind_chart=true so boxes/lines don't obscure candles (sample 09:19).
Reuse drawing objects: line.set_xy2 / box.set_right / label.set_x instead of delete+new on every update (sample 09:130-141, 2243-2246).
Mitigation color transition: separate mitBOXColor + MitBoxLabelColor + _applyMitStyle helper (sample 09:242-244, 663-668).
Highlight-on-touch: _applyHighlight changes bgcolor transparency when price enters box (sample 09:670-672).
isDark detection from chart.bg_color RGB to auto-flip text colors (sample 13:135-138).
Section toggles ①-㉗ grouped with circled numbers + inline inputs for compact settings UI (sample 09:21-33).
commonMistakes: No drawing cap → indicator silently stops rendering new objects after TV limit (50 default).
Delete+new every bar instead of set_* → memory churn, flicker, perf degradation.
Boxes drawn in front of candles → obscures price action.
Hardcoded text color (white) → invisible on light charts; no isDark detection.
Single mitigation color with no label color adjustment → mitigated boxes unreadable.
All inputs in one flat group → user can't find toggles; no section numbering.
Not declaring max_bars_back high enough → 'bars back limit' runtime error on long pivots.
Reusing the same drawing ID across modules without per-module arrays → clobbering.

gaps.currentIssue: indicator() declaration (line 18) lacks max_bars_back= parameter. With FVG/SMT arrays and request.security() chains, Pine can throw "index out of bounds" or "array too large" runtime error on deep history or low-liquidity symbols.
gaps.bestPractice: Samples 05 (line 7), 08 (line 2), 09 (line 17) all set max_bars_back=500 or 5000 in indicator() declaration to lock the historical lookback window before drawing/array logic accesses [i] indexing.
gaps.recommendedFix: Add max_bars_back=5000 to indicator() call alongside existing max_lines_count/max_boxes_count/max_labels_count=500. Single-line change; no logic impact.
gaps.expectedImpact: Eliminates intermittent runtime errors on deep history charts and pairs with sparse data (e.g. XAUUSD weekend gaps). Required for TradingView "publication-ready" status.

gaps.currentIssue: MSS detection (lines 172-183) uses raw close>lastSwingHigh without barstate.isconfirmed guard. Alert fires (or shape plots) on every realtime tick as price oscillates around the level, producing multiple MSS signals per real swing break.
gaps.bestPractice: Sample 08 (lines 378, 388) wraps MSS-style break logic in if ... and barstate.isconfirmed so the signal only finalizes once the bar closes. Sample 05 only paints structures on barstate.islast, never on realtime.
gaps.recommendedFix: Wrap mssBullNow/mssBearNow computation in if barstate.isconfirmed block (or add `mssBullNow and barstate.isconfirmed` filter in alert + plotshape gates). Mirrors the barstate.isconfirmed guard already used for FVG creation (line 227).
gaps.expectedImpact: Removes repaint on MSS alerts/webhooks; aligns MSS behaviour with FVG (which is already correctly gated). Critical for downstream orchestrator consuming JSON signals.

gaps.currentIssue: Indicator only exposes dynamic JSON via alert() (lines 305-342). No alertcondition() declarations anywhere — users cannot create alerts from TradingView's native Alert Dialog with a static message template. Breaks the standard TV UX for indicator-only subscribers.
gaps.bestPractice: Samples 05 (lines 1162-1188), 09 (lines 697-716), 12 (lines 876-895), 20 all provide BOTH alert() (dynamic JSON webhook) AND alertcondition() (static dialog). This dual-mode pattern is the de-facto standard for published indicators.
gaps.recommendedFix: Add 12 alertcondition() calls after the alert() block — one per signal (HTF_BIAS, DOL, SWEEP, MSS, IFVG, SMT, SB_TIME). Use constant strings as titles and short messages like 'YKP: MSS Bull — Body-close break above swing high'.
gaps.expectedImpact: Indicator becomes usable for non-webhook TV subscribers (chart-only users); also surfaces in TradingView's public alert list for community. Required for "invite-only" script acceptance.

gaps.currentIssue: Input i_fvgMitMode (line 32) is declared with options=["body","wick","50pct"] but never used — comment at line 223-224 explicitly states "Pine v5 doesn't allow dynamic string in if-chain inside loop cleanly". User toggling the option has zero effect on chart behaviour. This is a documented bug shipped to production.
gaps.bestPractice:
Sample 12 (lines 314-317) resolves identical problem cleanly with ternary at mitigation-source level:
bearishOrderBlockMitigationSource = orderBlockMitigationInput == CLOSE ? close : high
bullishOrderBlockMitigationSource = orderBlockMitigationInput == CLOSE ? close : low
Then uses the source variable inside the mitigation comparison.
gaps.recommendedFix: Replace close >= box.get_bottom(b) with `close >= (i_fvgMitMode == "body" ? math.max(open, close) : box.get_bottom(b))` style per-mode source variable. Define `float bullMitSrc = i_fvgMitMode == "body" ? math.max(close, open) : i_fvgMitMode == "wick" ? low : math.avg(box.get_top(b), box.get_bottom(b))`. Apply symmetrically for bearFvg.
gaps.expectedImpact: Removes silent dead-input (UX bug), honours user setting, expands indicator to wick/50pct mitigation modes other ICT scripts use. No new security calls.

gaps.currentIssue: FVG creation (lines 227-235) triggers on ANY 3-bar gap satisfying low > high[2] with zero size/quality threshold. On ranging/low-vol sessions this floods arrays with noise boxes (e.g. 1-pip FVGs on EURUSD). Causes alert spam and array thrash.
gaps.bestPractice:
Sample 05 (line 911) implements cumulative-delta auto-threshold:
threshold = fvg_auto ? ta.cum(math.abs(change_tf ? delta_per : 0)) / n * 2 : 0
Then requires `bullish_fvg_cnd := ... and delta_per > threshold and change_tf`. Drops weak FVG, keeps significant ones.
gaps.recommendedFix: Add i_fvgAutoThreshold = input.bool(true, ...) and compute FVG gap size as `(low - high[2]) / syminfo.mintick`. Reject FVG < threshold_ata(14)*0.5 (configurable). Mirror sample 05's `change_tf = timeframe.change(fvg_tf)` to avoid intra-TF duplicates.
gaps.expectedImpact: Cuts noisy FVG count by 50-80% on ranging pairs, reduces alert spam, improves webhook signal quality (Orchestrator receives only meaningful FVGs).

gaps.currentIssue: FVG detection hardcoded to current chart timeframe only (lines 228, 232). ICT playbook requires reading FVGs from HTF (H1/H4) while trading LTF (M15). Current implementation misses the most valuable FVG levels.
gaps.bestPractice: Sample 05 (lines 222, 904) uses input.timeframe('', "Timeframe", ...) and feeds it into request.security(syminfo.tickerid, fvg_tf, get_ohlc()). User can pivot FVG detection to HTF without leaving chart.
gaps.recommendedFix: Add i_fvgTf = input.timeframe("", "FVG timeframe", group="FVG", tooltip="Leave empty for current chart"). Inside the FVG creation block, replace `if low > high[2]` with `fvgLow > fvgHigh[2]` derived from `request.security(syminfo.tickerid, i_fvgTf, [low, high[2]], lookahead=barmerge.lookahead_on)`.
gaps.expectedImpact: Indicator becomes useful on M15 entries while keeping H4 FVG levels. Single biggest UX gap vs published SMC indicators like LuxAlgo.

gaps.currentIssue: Webhook JSON builder (line 77) uses raw string concatenation with str.tostring(year)+"-"+str.tostring(month)+"..." and hardcoded "#.########" price format. Timezone hardcoded to +07:00 in wibTimestamp() — incompatible with non-Jakarta users. Exchange/ticker symbol not in payload.
gaps.bestPractice: Sample 20 (line 43) uses str.format_time(time, "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss", "America/New_York") with IANA timezone string and str.tostring(_high, format.mintick) for price precision. Sample 09 includes syminfo.ticker and syminfo.prefix in payload.
gaps.recommendedFix: Replace wibTimestamp() with str.format_time(time, "yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss", i_sbTz). Replace str.tostring(close, "#.########") with str.tostring(close, format.mintick). Append '"ticker":"' + syminfo.ticker + '","exchange":"' + syminfo.prefix + '","exchange_tz":"' + i_sbTz + '"' to JSON.
gaps.expectedImpact: Webhook payload becomes timezone-agnostic (works for any user globally), uses symbol-correct precision, includes exchange for routing. Eliminates risk of orchestrator misinterpreting payload TZ.

gaps.currentIssue: Order Block drawing (lines 438-452) uses fixed displacement ATR multiple and creates box anchored to first available FVG. OB mitigation logic (implicit: delete when close exceeds) is hardcoded to close — no option for wick mitigation. OB also lacks "break + retest" mitigation pattern common in ICT tools.
gaps.bestPractice: Sample 12 (lines 102-103, 314-317) exposes orderBlockMitigationInput as input.string with options=[CLOSE, HIGHLOW] and routes to mitigationSource variable. Sample 05 implements proper break detection with `if close < array.get(iob_btm, index)` style array pruning (lines 776-806).
gaps.recommendedFix: Add i_obMitMode = input.string("Close", "OB mitigation", options=["Close","High/Low"], group="Order Blocks"). Replace `if close < ...` mitigation logic with mitSrc-based check matching sample 12's pattern. Add i_obShowBreak = input.bool(true, "Show break labels").
gaps.expectedImpact: Matches LuxAlgo SMC standard behaviour; users can tune OB invalidation to their preference. Required for OB to be publishable on TradingView.

gaps.currentIssue: nrSecurity() invoked 9 separate times: HTF pivot high, HTF pivot low, HTF close, corrClose, corrLow, corrHigh, PDH, PDL, PWH, PWL (lines 83-130). Each call consumes one of TV's 40-request budget per script. Inefficient.
gaps.bestPractice: Sample 07 (lines 110-115) batches HTF reads via tuple: htfFast = request.security(...); htfSlow = request.security(...). Sample 05 (line 904) batches 6-tuple: [src_c1, src_o1, src_h, src_l, src_h2, src_l2] = request.security(syminfo.tickerid, fvg_tf, get_ohlc()). Sample 09 uses [isclosed, closeAt, closedAtTime] tuples.
gaps.recommendedFix:
Combine into one tuple call:
[htfPh, htfPl, htfClose] = request.security(syminfo.tickerid, i_htf, [ta.pivothigh(high,i_lookback,i_lookback), ta.pivotlow(low,i_lookback,i_lookback), close], lookahead=barmerge.lookahead_on)
And similarly batch [corrClose, corrLow, corrHigh] and [pdh,pdl,pwh,pwl]. Reduces 9 calls to 3.
gaps.expectedImpact: Saves 6 request.security() slots (15% of TV budget), improves script load speed ~10-20%, leaves headroom for future MTF additions. Better Pine v6 dynamic_requests migration path.

gaps.currentIssue: Indicator only tracks Swing OB (line 438) — no Internal OB (smaller timeframe MSS-based OB). ICT playbook distinguishes Internal (lower TF precision entries) vs Swing OB (HTF structural levels). Missing ~50% of OB signal universe.
gaps.bestPractice:
Sample 12 and 05 implement BOTH:
- show_iob (internal) — derived from intermediate-term structure break
- show_ob (swing) — derived from swing structure break
Both are toggleable, independently coloured, independently limited (iob_showlast vs ob_showlast).
gaps.recommendedFix: Add separate internal OB pipeline. Use swing_length=3 for internal pivots (separate from i_lookback=5 for swing). Add i_maxIobBoxes=10 input. Compute internal OB at the `if not na(plSig)` internal block. Plot with distinct colour (e.g. lighter shade of bull/bear CSS).
gaps.expectedImpact: Doubles OB signal coverage (internal = entries, swing = targets). Matches LuxAlgo/GoldBot standard. Required for indicator to be competitive.

gaps.currentIssue: All state vars (lastHtfHigh, barsSinceSweepSsl, htfTrend, prevSbActive etc.) declared with `var` (lines 86-89, 99, 155, 192, 69). This means they only update on bar close. For real-time alerts on the forming bar, this causes 1-bar lag vs actual price action.
gaps.bestPractice: Sample 12 (line 297) uses `varip int currentBarIndex = bar_index` for real-time-tick state. `var` = persists across bars, updates on close. `varip` = persists in realtime, resets each bar. Use case-specific choice documented in samples 09.
gaps.recommendedFix: Add explicit `varip` for state that should update on each tick within forming bar (e.g. barsSinceSweepSsl during the forming bar, before MSS fires). Document the choice with `ponytail:` comment. Test: enable `barstate.isrealtime` debug plot to verify.
gaps.expectedImpact: Real-time intrabar signals now update as price moves (within same bar) instead of lagging 1 bar. Critical for scalping use case. Default `var` can stay for HTF bias (less repaint risk).

gaps.currentIssue: None of 16 input() calls (lines 23-43) provide `tooltip=` parameter. Users hovering over inputs see no explanation of what each setting does. Increases support load and lowers TV publishing rating.
gaps.bestPractice: Sample 12 (lines 56-75) defines all tooltip strings as constants at top, then attaches via tooltip= param on every input. Sample 05 (lines 14-34) uses 20+ tooltip strings. Sample 03 uses inline tooltip on critical inputs like tf_limit and cutoff.
gaps.recommendedFix: Add tooltip= to each input with Indonesian + English brief: e.g. input.session("1000-1100", "Asia SB window", tooltip="Asia Silver Bullet: 10:00-11:00 Asia/Jakarta = high-prob London open setup window", group="SB Windows"). Define tooltips as const at top for maintainability.
gaps.expectedImpact: Better UX, fewer user questions, higher TV publication rating (TV rewards scripts with tooltips in algorithm). Minimal code cost.

gaps.currentIssue: Related inputs use group= but no inline= parameter. Result: 16 inputs render as 16 vertical rows in Settings dialog, even when logically paired (e.g. i_smtEnabled + i_smtMinCorr belong on same row).
gaps.bestPractice: Sample 03 (lines 22-45) uses inline="ASIA" to put `use_asia`, `asia_text`, `asia`, `as_color` on one line. Sample 09 (line 94) and 20 use inline heavily to compact the dialog.
gaps.recommendedFix: Pair i_smtEnabled + i_smtMinCorr on inline="SMT". Pair i_asiaSession + i_londonSession + i_nySession inline="SB". Pair i_showDol + i_showPdhPdl inline="DOL". Saves ~6 vertical rows.
gaps.expectedImpact: Settings dialog 30% shorter, easier to scan, matches TV-published-script UX convention. Zero behaviour change.

gaps.currentIssue: FVG mitigation loop (lines 247-265) does array.clear(tempBullFvg) + for-loop push + reassign every bar. O(N) per bar where N = box count. Also creates then destroys temp arrays every tick.
gaps.bestPractice: Sample 05 (lines 773-806) iterates `for element in iob_type` and uses array.remove(iob_top, index) in-place. Sample 12 uses similar in-place pruning. No temp arrays.
gaps.recommendedFix:
Replace temp array approach with in-place reverse iteration:
for i = array.size(bullFvgBoxes) - 1 to 0
  b = array.get(bullFvgBoxes, i)
  if close < box.get_bottom(b)
    box.delete(b)
    array.remove(bullFvgBoxes, i)
Eliminates tempBullFvg/tempBearFvg arrays entirely.
gaps.expectedImpact: ~50% reduction in FVG-loop CPU per bar. Removes 2 var declarations. Safer under heavy box counts.

gaps.currentIssue: No license/author header at top of file. Lines 1-16 are version + prose but no Copyright/License. TradingView publication and most code-review checklists require explicit license.
gaps.bestPractice: Sample 12 (lines 1-2) starts with `// This work is licensed under a Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)` + author. Sample 20 (lines 1-7) cites authors + MPL 2.0.
gaps.expectedImpact: Required for IP protection. Also helps orchestrator detect version mismatch on webhook arrival (include version in JSON).

gaps.currentIssue: nrSecurity() wrapper (line 50) only specifies lookahead but not barmerge.gaps_off explicitly. Pine v5 default is gaps_off, but explicit declaration prevents behaviour drift on Pine v6 upgrade where defaults may differ.
gaps.bestPractice: Sample 03 (lines 226-228) explicitly writes: request.security(syminfo.tickerid, "D", open, barmerge.gaps_off, barmerge.lookahead_on). Sample 04-09 same.
gaps.recommendedFix:
Change nrSecurity() to:
nrSecurity(src, tf, exp) => request.security(src, tf, exp[1], barmerge.gaps_off, barmerge.lookahead_on)
Adds 1 explicit param.
gaps.expectedImpact: Future-proofs against Pine v6 default changes. Zero runtime impact today, but locks behaviour.

gaps.currentIssue: indicator() (line 18) does not declare dynamic_requests=true. Pine v6+ enforces dynamic requests for conditional request.security() (none used here) and benefits from declaring intent. TV also uses this flag for compilation hints.
gaps.bestPractice: Sample 20 (line 18) sets dynamic_requests = true explicitly. Sample 09 (line 12) same.
gaps.recommendedFix: Add , dynamic_requests=true to indicator() declaration. Single param.
gaps.expectedImpact: Forward-compatible with Pine v6 dynamic_requests enforcement; no current behaviour change. Required for clean Pine v6 migration.

gaps.currentIssue: Indicator has no timeframe guard (e.g. `if timeframe.in_seconds("") <= timeframe.in_seconds("60")` ). On Daily/Weekly charts, pivothigh(5,5) and FVG boxes render with weird scales, and request.security() HTF chaining creates infinite-loop edge cases.
gaps.bestPractice: Sample 03 (line 372) wraps entire core logic in `if timeframe.in_seconds("") <= timeframe.in_seconds(tf_limit)` where tf_limit is an input. Sample 07 same pattern.
gaps.recommendedFix: Wrap lines 82-458 in `if timeframe.isintraday` (or add i_tfLimit input). On D/W charts, plot a single label warning "Indicator designed for intraday". Preserves UX on all charts.
gaps.expectedImpact: Prevents broken visual output on higher TF charts. Reduces security call usage on D/W. Required polish for publishing.

gaps.currentIssue: Indicator has no Equal Highs/Lows (EQH/EQL) detection — a core ICT concept for liquidity stacking. Missing from signal set entirely.
gaps.bestPractice:
Sample 05 (lines 830-886) implements full EQH/EQL with:
- eq_len = input.int(3, "Bars Confirmation", ...)
- eq_threshold = input.float(0.1, ..., minval=0, maxval=0.5, step=0.1)
- Plot dotted lines + labels between consecutive equal highs/lows
- Trigger eqh_alert / eql_alert boolean for alert routing.
gaps.recommendedFix: Add EQH/EQL block after DOL section. Use ta.pivothigh(eq_len, eq_len) and compare current with previous using abs threshold via i_eqThreshold input. Add EQH_BULL/EQH_BEAR/EQL_BULL/EQL_BEAR to alert routing. ~30 lines.
gaps.expectedImpact: Adds 4 new signals. EQH/EQL is the #1 precursor to liquidity sweeps which the indicator already detects — natural extension. High signal quality in trending pairs.

gaps.currentIssue: Indicator lacks Premium/Discount zone visualization (50% equilibrium of recent range). ICT playbook uses this for entry filtering (buy discount, sell premium). User has no zone context.
gaps.bestPractice:
Sample 05 (lines 984-1033) and 02 (lines 34-41) implement:
- swingHigh = ta.highest(high, rangeLen)
- swingLow = ta.lowest(low, rangeLen)
- midpoint = (swingHigh + swingLow) / 2
- plot(midpoint) equilibrium line
- bgcolor premium/discount zones above/below
gaps.recommendedFix: Add i_showPremiumDiscount = input.bool(false, group="Zones"). Compute swingHigh/swingLow via ta.highest/lowest with i_pdzLength input. Plot equilibrium line + premium/discount bgcolor. ~15 lines.
gaps.expectedImpact: Adds major ICT visual context. Helps users filter setups (only buy in discount). Matches every published SMC indicator standard.

gaps.currentIssue: SMT logic (lines 292-300) only compares corrLow[1] vs corrLow[2] (single bar). Misses the "divergence over N-bar window" pattern that strong SMT signals exhibit. Also ignores correlation direction (positive vs negative correlation matters).
gaps.bestPractice: Sample 20 (lines 33, references) implements SMT with window-based divergence: checks if correlation pair failed to make N-bar high/low while primary did. Filters by correlation sign.
gaps.recommendedFix: Replace single-bar check with window: check if corr made N-bar high (corrHighest1 > corrHighest2) while primary did make new high. Add i_smtWindow = input.int(3, "SMT divergence window", minval=2, maxval=10). Use ta.highest(corrHigh, i_smtWindow)[1] comparison.
gaps.expectedImpact: Stronger SMT signals, fewer false positives. SMT already optional — quality matters more than quantity for this signal.

gaps.currentIssue: String literals ("BULL","BEAR","NEUTRAL", "body","wick","50pct") scattered through code. Constants like BULLISH = +1, BEARISH = -1 not used. Harder to grep/refactor.
gaps.bestPractice: Sample 12 (lines 9-54) defines all constants at top: BULLISH = +1, BULLISH_LEG = 1, GREEN = #089981, RED = #F23645, etc. Uses these throughout instead of magic strings.
gaps.recommendedFix:
Add at top after indicator():
BULL = 1
BEAR = -1
NEUTRAL = 0
FVG_MIT_BODY = "body"
FVG_MIT_WICK = "wick"
Use these instead of literals. Pure refactor, no logic change.
gaps.expectedImpact: Improves maintainability, easier to add new bias states (e.g. RANGING). Sets up for future Pine v6 enum support.

gaps.currentIssue: Helper functions (rising, fmt2, wibTimestamp, nrSecurity, buildJson) use standard function syntax. Pine v5 supports `method` keyword for UDT-style OOP, making related functions more readable.
gaps.bestPractice: Sample 09 (line 1047) uses method oldSwing(array<label> a, type) => for type-dispatched helpers. Improves self-documenting code.
gaps.recommendedFix: Convert nrSecurity to method form (optional). Replace `nrSecurity(src, tf, exp)` calls with explicit request.security inline. Lower priority — current function form is fine.
gaps.expectedImpact: Marginal readability gain. Skip unless other refactor triggers Pine v6 syntax check.

gaps.currentIssue: indicator() (line 18) does not set behind_chart=true. DOL lines + FVG boxes render in front of candles by default. Visually noisy.
gaps.bestPractice: Sample 20 (line 18) sets behind_chart = true for layered ICT visuals. FVG boxes + DOL lines render behind candles, more professional look.
gaps.recommendedFix: Add , behind_chart=true to indicator() declaration. Single param. Visual preference — test on chart before locking in.
gaps.expectedImpact: Cleaner visual layering matching published SMC indicators. One-line change.

gaps.currentIssue: i_sbTz input options (line 38) hardcodes 7 IANA zones. If user wants Asia/Singapore or Pacific/Auckland, no option. Also DST handling not documented.
gaps.bestPractice: Sample 03 (line 9) provides 27 GMT offset options covering +/-14. Sample 09 (line 1383) uses America/New_York in time() function. Both expose timezone as freeform string with explanation.
gaps.recommendedFix: Change i_sbTz to input.string("Asia/Jakarta", "Timezone (IANA)", tooltip="Any IANA timezone. Examples: Asia/Singapore, Europe/Berlin, America/Chicago. Or use Etc/GMT+N format."). Pine v5 time() accepts any IANA string.
gaps.expectedImpact: Eliminates user request for adding timezones. One-line input change.

gaps.currentIssue: buildJson() (line 77) embeds no version field. When orchestrator receives webhook, it cannot detect schema version mismatch (e.g. consumer running v1 expects fields current code dropped).
gaps.bestPractice: Sample 20 includes semantic event type in payload. Standard practice for webhook contracts includes a schema_version field.
gaps.recommendedFix: Prepend schema_version:1 to JSON: '{"schema":"ykp-ict-sb-v1","source":"tradingview",...}. Add CHANGELOG.md documenting field additions/removals.
gaps.expectedImpact: Future-proofs orchestrator contract. One JSON field added. Critical for v3+ migration safety.

gaps.currentIssue: FVG boxes anchored to formation (line 243-244 comment) — fixed. Cannot extend to current bar or N bars ahead. Limits visual context.
gaps.bestPractice: Sample 05 (line 232) fvg_extend = input.int(1, "Extend FVG", minval = 0). Sample 20 extends FVG boxes to right via box.set_right(bar_index + fvg_extend).
gaps.recommendedFix: Add i_fvgExtend = input.int(0, "Extend FVG bars", minval=0, maxval=50, group="FVG"). In the FVG drawing block, change `right=time` to `right=time + i_fvgExtend * timeframe.in_seconds() * 1000`.
gaps.expectedImpact: User-tunable FVG visualisation. Optional cosmetic feature.

gaps.currentIssue: No documented test/publish checklist in file. After changes, no way to verify Pine v5/v6 compat, no lint pass, no TradingView publication criteria check.
gaps.bestPractice: Sample 12 includes @variable documentation comments (e.g. line 314-315) that double as inline docs. Sample 09 follows PineCoders rubric (https://www.pinecoders.com/techniques/linting/).
gaps.recommendedFix: Add final section "// === PINE CODERS RUBRIC SELF-CHECK ===" with assertions: max_boxes_count OK, no repaint in realtime, var vs varip intentional, etc. Or add a separate test.pine that loads the indicator and verifies state via plot.

verdicts: GAP 1 (Timezone SB via input.session + IANA): KEEP. Verified — samples only use input.session without IANA TZ arg in time(); playerjohnson hardcodes America/New_York. v2 genuinely more robust. Claim accurate.
GAP 2 (No-repaint nrSecurity exp[1]+lookahead_on): KEEP. Verified — only 3/20 samples use lookahead_on; none wrap it consistently. v2 wrapper is cleaner and applied uniformly. Claim accurate.
GAP 3 (alert.freq_once_per_bar_close): KEEP. Verified — zero samples use once_per_bar_close; all use once_per_bar or default. v2 fix is real and superior for signal integrity.
GAP 4 (MSS body-close break vs wick): KEEP. Valid ICT pattern, toggle-able. Low risk, real benefit.
GAP 5 (Sweep TTL reset after MSS): KEEP. Pro pattern, prevents multi-MSS from one sweep. Sound.

GAP 6 (FVG array FIFO + body mitigation): KEEP but DOWNGRADE claim. Not novel — 15/20 samples use box arrays. v2 is standard, not a v1-fix-from-research. Accurate as a refactor, overclaim as research-derived.

GAP 7 (HTF BOS/CHoCH state machine vs HH/HL): MODIFY framing. MarcosACH/19 uses function-based CHoCH of equal sophistication. v2 inline var-int approach is an alternative, NOT superior. README 'more pro' framing overclaims — reword to 'alternative non-repaint implementation'.

GAP 8 (SMT correlation filter |corr|>=0.6): MODIFY framing. Zero of 20 samples use ta.correlation for SMT — this is original work, not 'professional pattern research'. Keep the feature (genuine value: filters weak SMT), but drop the 'research-derived pro pattern' claim. Mark as v2-original addition.

README claim 'Riset dari 8+ professional-grade repos': MODIFY. Changelog cites 8 repos but 4 (btankutt, 0xSHAK1B, jchi18, BAKOME) are absent from samples folder — cannot verify they informed the code. Either fetch those repos or reduce the citation list to the 4 actually present (yusin99, VitaHoang, craftzbay, orestefrison).

FVG mitigation mode selector (body/wick/50pct) input: DROP. Only 'body' is implemented; wick/50pct are dead options ('reserved for future'). YAGNI — remove the input, hardcode body, add ponytail: comment naming the upgrade path. Dead config = complexity without benefit.
PDH/PDL/PWH/PWL lines (toggle off default): KEEP. Pure optional visual, zero runtime cost when off, no complexity bloat. Fine.
OB displacement ATR multiple input + max OB boxes: KEEP. Standard, useful, bounded.
Duplicate FVG cap (lines 218-221 AND 238-241): DROP one. Dead code — the second cap block runs after push and is redundant with the first. Remove lines 238-241.
News block moved to Orchestrator: KEEP. Correct boundary — Pine cannot fetch external API. Sound architectural call.
Webhook JSON with bar_index dedup: KEEP. Genuinely useful for Orchestrator idempotency, not present in samples.
strengthsToPreserve: Explicit no-repaint tradeoff disclosure in README (1-bar lag) — keep this honesty, it is rarer than the code fix itself.
All signal alerts funnel through one buildJson() function + single rising() guard — consistent, auditable, easy to extend.
TTL/counter logic for sweep → MSS → IFVG is sound and prevents stale confluence triggers.
Inputs are grouped and bounded (minval/maxval) — no unbounded user damage.
Optional layers (OB, PDH/PDL) default off — good minimalism principle.
finalRecommendations: Edit README: shrink repo citation list to actually-fetched samples; reword GAP 7 and GAP 8 as 'alternative' and 'original' respectively.
Edit sri-ict-silver-bullet.pine: remove lines 238-241 (redundant FVG cap); remove i_fvgMitMode input and hardcode body-close; add ponytail comment for wick/50pct future upgrade.
Run Pine syntax/visual sanity check: verify no runtime error from box.set_bgcolor(na) on hidden boxes; confirm array mutation order on realtime bar before declaring v2 final.
